title: PSA: Have you heard of trade dress protection laws? Now you have.
author: LiquidZebra
selftext:
Had to ask AI, found a new legal term. Ask yourself: what game is displayed here? 

From the [https://www.finnegan.com/en/insights/articles/a-guide-to-trade-dress-in-the-united-states.html](https://www.finnegan.com/en/insights/articles/a-guide-to-trade-dress-in-the-united-states.html)

(4) whether it was capable of creating a commercial impression distinct from the accompanying words.

If it is **recognized to be inherently distinctive** then the trade dress may be protected, if it is not recognized then secondary meaning must be proven, which will mean that the consuming public can identify the origin of the goods or services based on the packaging alone. The factors to be considered are:

1) Direct consumer testimonials.

2) Consumer surveys.

3) The amount and form of advertising.

4) Sales volume and length.

5) Form of use.



**TL;DR:** Copying a right-side dialogue layout and menu order is legal, but replicating *Disco Elysium*’s exact typography, layout proportions, and near-identical briefcase and spiral-notebook icons puts this squarely in the **copyright and trade dress danger zone**—even with the added parchment border.
